edges: The plain maskray primarily feeds on caridean shrimp and polychaete worms.
Peter Last authored the first scientific description of the plain maskray.
The plain maskray and the Ningaloo maskray are the most basal members of the genus Neotrygon.
The plain maskray is threatened by incidental capture in commercial bottom trawl fisheries.
The plain maskray is parasitized by the tapeworm Acanthobothrium jonesi.
Historically, the plain maskray may have been negatively affected by intensive fishing by Japanese, Chinese, and Taiwanese trawlers.
